Home.title: Atlas

SignIn.title: Sign in to Atlas
SignIn.invalidCredentials: The email or password is incorrect.
SignIn.unavailable: Sign-in is not available right now. Please try again later.

Progress.title: Project progress
Progress.subtitle: Where Atlas stands on its roadmap. Updated on {date}.
Progress.waitingIntro: Only you can do these; each one unblocks a step.

NoAccess.title: No access
NoAccess.body: Your account is suspended or no longer exists. Ask an Admin of your organization if you think this is a mistake.

Errors.noCredit: No license credit remains. Ask Atlas for more licenses, or request the deletion of an account you no longer need.
Errors.emailUnavailable: This e-mail address cannot be used. Use another address.
Errors.lastAdmin: The organization must keep at least one active Admin.
Errors.notYourself: You cannot do this on your own account; another Admin must do it.
Errors.creditsBelowAccounts: Credits cannot go below the number of accounts. The customer must first request deletions.
Errors.minimumCredit: An organization starts with at least 1 credit.
Errors.deletionPending: Cancel the deletion request before reactivating this account.
Errors.forbidden: You are not allowed to do this.
Errors.expiredLink: This link has expired or was already used.
Errors.invalid: Some values are missing or not valid. Check the form and try again.
Errors.unavailable: Atlas cannot do this right now. Please try again in a moment.
Errors.archived: This project is archived: restore it before changing it.
Errors.idTaken: This identifier is already used in this project.
Errors.invalidId: Use lowercase letters, digits, _ and - only.

Projects.title: Projects
Projects.name: Name
Projects.descriptionHint: What the project is for, e.g. “Multi-ERP consolidation 2027”.
Projects.emptyHint: Create the first project of your organization.
Projects.emptyViewer: No project has been shared yet.

Project.problemCounts: {errors, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}} · {warnings, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}
Project.startBody: Describe the systems the project reads (ERP, MES…) and their tables: by hand, or by importing a dictionary file.
Project.comingNext: Models, rules, value mappings, history and downloads arrive in the next steps of this phase.

Accounts.title: Licenses and accounts
Accounts.subtitle: Each account uses one license credit, whatever its status, until its deletion is validated.
Accounts.newDescription: The person receives an e-mail to choose a password. The account uses one credit at once.
Accounts.name: Name
Accounts.suspendBody: They are signed out at once and can no longer open Atlas. The license credit stays used; you can reactivate the account later.
Accounts.deleteBody: The account is suspended at once. Atlas then removes it and gives the credit back. You can cancel the request until then. Their past changes stay in the history with their name.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.name: Name
Profile.sessionsBody: Signs you out of Atlas on every other browser and device.

Invite.title: Join Atlas
Invite.invalid: This invitation link has expired or was already used. Ask the Admin of your organization to send it again.
Invite.intro: You are invited with {email}. Choose your name as colleagues will see it, and a password.
Invite.name: Name

Reset.title: Forgotten password
Reset.intro: Enter the e-mail address of your account. We send you a link to choose a new password.
Reset.expired: This link has expired or was already used. Ask for a new one.
Reset.sent: If an account exists for this address, an e-mail with a link has been sent. Check your inbox.

Control.title: Organizations
Control.subtitle: Licensing figures only: Atlas never shows projects, people or content of a customer.
Control.newDescription: Atlas invites the customer's first Admin by e-mail; the invitation uses the first credit.
Control.name: Name
Control.adminEmailHint: Usually the customer's contact person. The control tower does not keep this address.
Control.inviteFailed: The organization was created, but the invitation of its first Admin could not be sent. Try again below.
Control.creditsHint: At least {accounts}, the number of accounts that exist.
Control.deletionsCount: {count, plural, =0 {No account waits for deletion.} one {# account waits for deletion.} other {# accounts wait for deletion.}}
Control.deletionsHint: Which accounts they are stays with the customer.
Control.validateBody: The accounts are removed for good and their credits go back to the organization.
Control.deletionValidated: 1 account removed; its credit is back.
Control.deletionsValidated: Accounts removed; their credits are back.
Control.firstAdminBody: This organization has no account yet. Invite its first Admin.
Control.auditSubtitle: Every action of the operator, kept for good.

audit.deletions_validated: {count, plural, one {# deletion validated} other {# deletions validated}}

Sources.title: Sources
Sources.subtitle: The systems this project reads and the description of their tables. Metadata only: Atlas never reads your data.
Sources.systemHint: A source system, e.g. one ERP instance. Two instances of the same product are two systems.
Sources.systemIdHint: Lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, e.g. sap_fr. It cannot change later.
Sources.productHint: e.g. SAP S/4HANA 2023, Oracle E-Business Suite 12.2
Sources.landingHint: Where this system's raw data lands in the warehouse; the generated code reads from there.
Sources.deleteSystemBody: The system and its datasets leave the project. They stay in the history and can be restored. Mappings that read them will show errors.
Sources.newDatasetHint: A table, view or file of this system, entered by hand. You fill its columns next.
Sources.datasetNameHint: As in the source, e.g. KNA1.
Sources.copyHint: The systems and their datasets are copied into this project; the copies are then independent.
Sources.datasetCount: {count, plural, =0 {no dataset} one {# dataset} other {# datasets}}
Sources.copiedSome: Copied, except the systems already in this project.
Sources.emptyBody: Add the first system this project reads, then describe its tables by hand or import a dictionary.
Sources.emptyViewer: No source has been described yet.

Dataset.deleteBody: The dataset leaves the project. It stays in the history and can be restored. Mappings that read it will show errors.
Dataset.landingNameHint: Only when it differs from the system's naming pattern.
Dataset.pasteHint: Tip: paste rows copied from a spreadsheet into the grid (column, native type, nullable, key position, description).
Dataset.dialectHint: Used to translate native types into Atlas types.
Dataset.name: Column
Dataset.unknownType: Unknown native type: choose the Atlas type.
Dataset.noColumn: No column yet: add one, or paste rows from a spreadsheet.

Import.title: Import a dictionary
Import.subtitle: Describe many tables at once from a file listing their columns. Only metadata: no data is read.
Import.noSystem: Create a system first: the import fills the datasets of one system.
Import.step1Body: Run the query of your database with your own tools and access, and save the result as CSV (or Excel). Atlas never connects to your systems.
Import.otherSources: Any file with the columns dataset, column, native_type (and optionally nullable, primary_key_position, description, dataset_description, namespace) works, e.g. an export of an ERP data dictionary.
Import.dialectHint: Translates native types into Atlas types.
Import.fileHint: CSV (comma or semicolon) or Excel .xlsx, up to 20 MB. Read in your browser only.
Import.tooLarge: The file is larger than 20 MB.
Import.unreadable: This file cannot be read. Save it as CSV (UTF-8) or Excel .xlsx.
Import.empty: The file has no row under its header.
Import.missingList: Kept, as they are not in the file (never deleted silently): {list}
Import.done: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing changed: the datasets were already up to date.} one {# dataset saved.} other {# datasets saved.}}
